ad7c7c7379.why: Both judge lows fixed: 'spins a web' no longer claims the first web is wheel-shaped, and 'It copied a web it found nearby' is a live learning lure, false because spiders build working webs without observation. Mother dies after laying (late autumn to early winter), young hatch in spring and disperse: checked. In lane (instinct example, TEKS 5.13B).

d13dab9ea2.why: The high tell is gone: the stem no longer names the instinct, and every choice is a claim about the mother, each lure putting her on hand, so the 'no one to teach' reasoning eliminates none of them; only knowing she leaves does. Mother covers the nest and returns to sea, incubation 45-70 days (about 60), no parental care, night emergence, brightest horizon: checked. Lane as the judge ruled (the absence is why the instinct matters).

5707d900a7.why: Context now 'look both ways, and then again', true under either traffic side (Kerb Drill right-left-right; today's Green Cross Code 'look all around'). 'Jerking back a hand that touches a hot pan' is plainly the withdrawal reflex (involuntary, spinal). Sneeze and cough reflexes unchanged and true.

4d7ce512e6.why: Context error fixed: it now says a learned behaviour is not inherited and each puppy must learn the trick, which is true (acquired traits are not passed on through reproduction; puppies can still learn socially). The two falling-together 'inborn' lures are now one; 'It practises the trick on its own' is false (tricks come from reinforcement or observation, never solo practice). Choices parallel, 32-34 characters.

fd8d06002c.why: Both clarity lows fixed and true: the blue tit is 'a small passerine bird', and the cream sat at the top under the foil. No date added, so the waxboard detail is safe. The judge's third low (the weak lure 'get by without any instincts') remains, but two lures stay live, so not a drop.

61b71e1584.why: Key now 'The colour of her eyes', 21 characters against 21-23, so no longer the short standout; 'Her skill at the piano' removes the echo of adaptations' swimming lure and is an acquired skill. Eye colour genetic; language, skill and scar acquired: checked.

90ea79e4bf.why: Facts hold (riding is procedural memory, practised, lasting; not inborn, not inherited), but the key is a standout: only it answers the stem's set-up ('however easy it feels' echoes 'as easily as he breathes'), with the corrective 'still', and it is the longest choice. Two lures fall to everyday knowledge (every child learned to ride, so no baby is born able to, the blacksmith's flaw; 'you never forget how to ride a bike'), leaving only the instinct lure live.
